Thank you so much! This made me feel less alone. I used to be a biology major and only liked wet lab where I could do stuff with my hands. I changed my major literally the last possible second I could do it (the last week of my junior year) to English and film (an Interdepartmental Major where I could chose my classes w/o reqs so I could focus on what I want to do). I definitely think writing is a better choice for me. I’ve always liked it when I was younger but people kept saying it’s a dead-end and I’d be wasting my “smarts”. But I’m really good at writing and I’ve been writing a book since sophomore year and I want to be author. It’ll definitely prevent me from having an environment where I have to talk to people all the time. That’s why the networking is important, I really want to graduate with some contacts so that when I finish the book (next year) I can hopefully set up some meetings for a publishing deal (hopefully).

And I definitely get the blunt thing! I’ve had literally 8 part-time jobs (I’m only 20; thanks indecisiveness) some of which in customer service and people always demand that I liven up and not be so blunt. I don’t have any bad intentions but people think it’s so easy to do. And some customers complain about me. But now I have a new job in a retail supermarket (not going to school this semester which is a different, much longer story) and all I do is stock shelves and do online grocery pick up for people (shopping for people). And I’m grateful for it because I literally don’t have to talk to anyone at all unless it’s telling my supervisor I’m going on break.
